_comment: Publisher country inference, for the secondary salience term in HANDOFF.md §2.5:
salience = log1p(distinct_domains) + 0.5 * log1p(distinct_source_countries)
It says a story crossed borders. It never routes a story anywhere — there is one
content model — and it is weighted half of the domain term.
Resolution order, implemented in worker/refdata.ts:
1. exact domain match in `domains` below
2. the domain's ccTLD, via `cctldExceptions` or the ISO code itself
3. UNKNOWN — and unknown is EXCLUDED from the distinct count, not bucketed
as a country of its own. Bucketing would make every unresolved domain look
like it shared a nationality, which is the one wrong answer available.
KNOWN LIMITATION, measured 2026-08-11 rather than assumed. In the cached bundles
the generic-TLD tail is overwhelmingly US LOCAL BROADCAST STATIONS — wcvb, wral,
wlky, wsls, azfamily, abc3340, kshb, fox29, wvtm13, 4029tv and hundreds more, each
appearing 7-15 times. There is no list that covers them and no honest pattern rule
(the w-/k- call-sign convention would misfire on ordinary words). So US-domestic
breadth is UNDER-counted while international spread is counted correctly.
That bias runs in the direction the signal wants: a story carried in five countries
still scores its five, and a story carried by five US stations scores the domains
it earned without also collecting a border-crossing bonus it did not. The domain
term is 2:1 dominant regardless. worker/run.ts reports resolution coverage in the
run summary so this stays visible instead of silently decaying.
